ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Tetracyclines: 5

A bacterial isolate was previously inhibited by tetracycline but now maintains a much lower intracellular antibiotic concentration. Testing shows an increased membrane transport process that exports the drug. Which resistance mechanism best explains the change?

  1. High oral bioavailability
  2. Oxygen-dependent bacterial uptake
  3. Alteration of the ribosomal binding site
  4. Increased bacterial drug efflux
  5. Poor systemic absorption after oral administration
Answer and explanation

Increased bacterial drug efflux

Efflux can lower intracellular tetracycline concentrations and cause resistance.

Option explanations

Increased bacterial drug efflux: Efflux can lower intracellular tetracycline concentrations and cause resistance.

Poor systemic absorption after oral administration: Oral vancomycin acts mainly in the bowel and does not provide dependable systemic therapy. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

High oral bioavailability: Linezolid has high oral bioavailability, permitting an appropriate IV-to-oral switch in selected stable patients. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Oxygen-dependent bacterial uptake: Aminoglycosides require active oxygen-dependent transport into susceptible bacteria. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Alteration of the ribosomal binding site: Ribosomal methylation or other target changes can reduce binding of some protein-synthesis inhibitors. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
